correctness.rationale: Uniform marks hit a given j-set with probability q_j, so each label has finite stationary age and independent Brownian increments conditional on the ages with variances 2DA_i. The marked-Poisson void exponent for arbitrary age thresholds is r times the mean over marks of the maximum touched threshold. Convexity and exchangeability give the lower bound rq_j/j times the sum of thresholds; exchangeable hit-count increments q_j−q_{j−1}=q_1 (N−m)_{j−1}/(N−1)_{j−1} (falling factorials) are nonincreasing, so the bound with c=rq_k/k applies for each subset of tags. Expanding the exponential moment into nonnegative orthant integrals gives finiteness for 0<θ<c, with nonpositive θ automatic. The event of no tagged hit for s/k units has probability exp(−cs) and implies the age sum exceeds s up to a null boundary, so the moment diverges at and above c. Independently, scanning backward until the next hit of the j unresolved labels gives a waiting time Exp(rq_j), independent of the hit mark, and adds j times that wait to the age sum before removing hit labels. This recursion also gives finiteness exactly when θ<min_{j reachable}rq_j/j=c; initial j=k is always present. It reproduces the stated pair transform, with rates for hitting one particular label only λ₂−λ₁ and for hitting both 2λ₁−λ₂. For the excursion, conditional Gaussian tails plus Cauchy–Schwarz bound the probability by 2^k E exp(−k²z²/(4DS_k)); the finite age moment and AM–GM give exponential rate at least k sqrt(c/D). With a common age floor az, the probability is bounded below by exp(−rq_kaz) times erfc(sqrt(z/(4Da)))^k. Optimization of rq_ka+k/(4Da) matches the upper probability bound on the logarithmic scale. This uses fixed N,m,k,r,D and no first-passage interpretation. Finally the exact falling-factorial sum for q_k/q_1 has nonincreasing terms in m and a strictly decreasing j=1 term for k≥2; it gives precisely the endpoint ratios k and sqrt(k). An independently written rational calculation using literal subset marks and the backward-cover recursion (`python3 -B /workspace/branches/bounded_review_checks.py 5`) checked hit counts, strict normalized order and age transforms for N=2 through 10; the frozen floating-point and quadrature script was inspected, not executed. The finite checks are not used to prove the asymptotics.

evidence: The exact pair density is prior coverage of the underlying distribution; the retrieved large-distance connected pair-density statement concerns G(0,v) in a large-N treatment, one coordinate at the origin, not two simultaneous absolute excursions at finite fixed N.
The source describes nonmonotone covariance amplitude in m for N>6. Normalized equal-threshold rates depend on q_k/q_1, a different quantity.

A classical shock representation supplies the age vector, but the excursion result requires balancing the cost of the common lower age floor against the independent Gaussian fluctuations and proving that asynchronous ages cannot lower the rate.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Covariance nonmonotonicity neither implies nor contradicts normalized orthant monotonicity. Age survival by itself does not determine excursion asymptotics without the Brownian step; the known exact pair law can also yield asymptotics by analysis but is not an all-k theorem incorporating them. No stronger already-evaluated result was established with these same premises and conclusions.

evidence: Poisson thinning by reset mark gives independent exponential backward first times for each exact shock type; the tagged ages are their componentwise minima, the classical Marshall–Olkin law. Equation (1.1) of arXiv:2004.11241v1 explicitly presents this construction for a pair.
The source batch-reset model gives exact two-point positional data; the stated theorem integrates an absolute orthant in which every tagged coordinate exceeds the same moving threshold.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An age survival law is equivalent to the shock minima distribution, not to the tail of the Gaussian mixture of those ages. The two-point position law materially overlaps and could be analyzed for k=2, but the full claim includes all tagged subsets and strict batch normalization.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the equal-threshold fixed-finite-N all-k excursion rate and the strict normalized comparison for uniform partial batches. The marked-age law itself is a classical shock-model law and the positional hierarchy and exact two-point distribution are prior work. The claimed Gaussian-mixture logarithmic orthant asymptotic and its batch ordering are not stated by those results in the inspected material; in particular a positional Fourier recursion or the domain of its exponential moments does not by itself provide the matching joint lower tail bound. The auxiliary moment threshold is an exact extraction from the known shock-age structure, not a claim to have introduced that structure or its fully synchronized endpoint.
residual_risks: The stationary Fourier hierarchy and known multivariate exponential/shock theory enable further implicit extractions. A general theorem for these correlated-variance Gaussian mixtures or an uninspected positional asymptotic may subsume all or part of the result.
No local published-catalog comparison was possible. The bounded search and scope distinctions are not a proof of priority.

value.rationale: The result isolates a large-excursion observable whose marginal-normalized rate orders every batch size even though covariance amplitude may behave differently. It identifies the common reset hiatus as a sharp mechanism for simultaneous rare displacements and provides a precise diagnostic for all k at finite N, not just a fit at one threshold. It does not claim a prefactor, a first-passage law or a large-N uniform limit.
